Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The cited World Bank/TradingEconomics figure (rural access 24.99% in 2021, sourced from World Bank SDG7 tracking) is consistent with a separate World Bank project document (P181221) which puts urban access at 93.1% and rural access at ~25% for 2021, an ~68pp gap. The World Bank's Botswana National Energy Compact (dated 2024/2025) confirms the disparity persists: national access reached 76.6% by 2024/2025, with urban areas (Gaborone, Jwaneng) exceeding 90% while rural communities have remained 'relatively unchanged over the past decade'. This keeps the gap firmly above 60 percentage points, supporting Value Code 1.
revised_comments: Botswana shows a stark urban-rural electrification divide. World Bank data (SDG7 tracking, via national project documents) records urban electricity access at around 93% versus rural access of roughly 25%, a gap of some 68 percentage points as of 2021. The World Bank's 2024/2025 National Energy Compact for Botswana confirms this disparity persists: overall national access reached 76.6%, with urban centres such as Gaborone and Jwaneng exceeding 90% coverage while rural communities have seen little change over the past decade, remaining well below 60% access. The gap therefore continues to exceed 60 percentage points.
